# Runledger LLM Integration Summary

Runledger is a Rust workspace for durable jobs, workflow orchestration, and
worker runtime loops on PostgreSQL.

This file is for downstream agents integrating Runledger into another
application. It is not an AGENTS.md file and should not be treated as maintainer
instructions for this repository.

## Imports

```rust
use runledger_core::prelude::*;
use runledger_postgres::prelude::*;
use runledger_runtime::prelude::*;
```

The preludes intentionally avoid generic `Result` and `Error` aliases so they
can be imported together.

## Choose The API

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One independent retried unit of work | `enqueue_job` with `JobEnqueue` |
| Multi-step work with dependencies | `WorkflowDagBuilder` (simple) or workflow run/step builders (advanced) |
| Multi-step work with a durable JSON result | Declare a result step and use workflow handle APIs |
| Fan-out, fan-in, or ordered stages | `WorkflowDagBuilder::after_success` / `after_terminal` |
| Human/API approval or another external gate | External workflow steps |
| Delayed or recurring entrypoint | `upsert_job_schedule` with `JobScheduleUpsert` |
| Worker process lifecycle | `Supervisor::run_until_shutdown` |
| Admin/status views | `get_*` and `list_*` APIs in `runledger_postgres::jobs` |

Use `set_job_schedule_active` to pause/resume schedules and
`set_job_schedule_next_fire_at` to retime a schedule cursor.

## Workflow DAG Rule

If work has step dependencies, build a workflow DAG:

```rust
let run = WorkflowDagBuilder::new("workflow.example", &metadata)
    .job("a", "jobs.a", &payload_a)?
    .job("b", "jobs.b", &payload_b)?
    .after_success("b", ["a"])?
    .build()?;

enqueue_workflow_run(&pool, &run).await?;
```

For workflows that should return a durable JSON result, declare one initial DAG
step as the result step with `.result_step(...)` or `.try_result_step_key(...)`,
enqueue with `enqueue_workflow_run_handle`, and wait/read through
`WorkflowRunHandle::get_result`. Handler success returns `JobCompletion`; use
`JobCompletion::with_output(...)` for compact result metadata. Prefer explicit
wait timeouts in production. The default waits up to five minutes. `timeout: None`
opts into unbounded waits and may hold a PostgreSQL listener connection.

Use `WorkflowRunEnqueueBuilder` and `WorkflowStepEnqueueBuilder` for advanced per-step
settings, external steps, or hand-authored dependency specs.

`WorkflowDagBuilder` validates workflow shape, not job registration. `.job(...)`
fails immediately for blank step keys, blank job types, and duplicate step keys.
`.after_success(...)` / `.after_terminal(...)` fail immediately for blank
identifiers or an unknown target step. Missing prerequisites, self-dependencies,
duplicate dependencies, cycles, empty step lists, blank workflow types from
`new(...)`, and blank idempotency keys fail at `.build()` / `.try_build()`.
Use lower-level builders when call sites should pass explicit `StepKey` and
`JobType` values.

Do not manually orchestrate ordinary workflows by polling job status, enqueueing
dependent jobs from parent handlers, encoding dependency state in payload JSON,
or adding app-owned workflow edge tables.

## Worker Runtime Rule

Use `Supervisor::run_until_shutdown` for ordinary worker binaries:

```rust
let supervisor = Supervisor::builder(&pool, JobsConfig::from_env())?
    .with_registry(registry)
    .build()?;

supervisor
    .run_until_shutdown(shutdown_signal, std::time::Duration::from_secs(30))
    .await?;
```

Use `worker::run_worker_loop`, `scheduler::run_scheduler_loop`, and
`reaper::run_reaper_loop` only for custom runtime orchestration.

## Error Handling

For public surfaces, return `QueryError::code()` and
`QueryError::client_message()`. Use `QueryError::internal_message()` only for
trusted diagnostics.
